land.text: the three governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok; 'Iraqi troops were withdrawn from the Kurdish regions in October 1991' (Operation Provide Comfort page)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row (1960-2005) still draws the Kurdish north; the iraqi-republic dossier carries the 1992 loss. No state held the land between the October 1991 withdrawal and the 19 May 1992 elections.

capitals.name: Erbil (Hewlêr)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Erbil'. From 1996 to 2006 the PUK ran a separate administration around Sulaymaniyah; the Kurdistan Region page says only that the two zones 'reunified in 2006'.

correction.text: the three governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok, 'Autonomy founded: 19 May 1992'; Halabja later a fourth governorate within Sulaymaniyah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the Iraqi Republic row draws the north as Iraqi). The three governorates come to about 36,900 km2 by cells against the infobox 'Total: 46,862 km2' (the page gives no year; ratio 0.79, within a factor of two; the page does not break the figure down). The 'Green Line' is not defined by any page opened. The Operation Provide Comfort page (6 April 1991, no-fly zone north of the 36th parallel, Iraqi withdrawal October 1991) explains how the line arose.

correction.text: the Region after the Peshmerga took 'most disputed areas, including Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar and Makhmur' in June 2014

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, June 2014 to 16 October 2017. Sinjar was lost to ISIL in early August 2014 and retaken on 13 November 2015 (ledger), so the Sinjar part holds only 2014-06..2014-07 and 2015-11 onward. The 2017 page says the Region 'lost 40% of the land mass it had administered prior to the conflict', and a later sentence says 'a fifth'; neither gives km2.

correction.text: the Region back to the three governorates after Iraq's October 2017 advance; the disputed territories 'remain contested'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On 31 October [Abadi] announced Iraq had regained control of all disputed areas'; the page does not name the line afterwards (the pre-June-2014 line, 'the Green Line', is not defined on the pages opened). Halabja Governorate sits inside the Sulaymaniyah cells.

region.text: the governorates of Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Duhok

ledger.note: 19 May 1992: the Kurdistan Region holds its first elections. Infobox 'Autonomy founded: 19 May 1992'; 'The first elections, held on 19 May 1992'; the KDP won 45.3% and the first cabinet under Fuad Masum followed in July. Iraqi troops had been withdrawn from the Kurdish regions in October 1991 (Operation Provide Comfort page).

15 October 2005: the Region becomes a federal region of Iraq. Infobox 'Federal region established: 15 October 2005'; the page says the new government recognized Kurdish autonomy 'in 2005 in the new Iraqi constitution'. No land changes hands; the republic-of-iraq dossier records this as a 2005 gain of the Region (see notes).
13 June 2014: Kurdish forces take Kirkuk. The Northern Iraq offensive page: 'Kurdish forces took the city on 13 June, after government forces abandoned their posts'.

region.text: Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar and Makhmur

ledger.note: June 2014: the Peshmerga take the disputed areas. 'Due to the Iraqi withdrawal, Kurdish Peshmerga took control of most disputed areas, including Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar and Makhmur.' The page ties the move to the Islamic State invasion 'in June 2014' without a day.
early August 2014: ISIL takes Sinjar. The Northern Iraq offensive page: ISIL 'captured the town in early August 2014'; the War in Iraq page: 'ISIL captured Sinjar after the Peshmerga abandoned it'.
13 November 2015: Kurdish forces retake Sinjar. 'ISIL lost Sinjar on 13 November, to Kurdish forces'; the Peshmerga offensive had begun on 17 December 2014.

region.text: Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar and Makhmur: the disputed territories

ledger.note: 15-16 October 2017: Iraq moves on the disputed territories. The conflict 'began on 15 October 2017 after tensions arising from the Kurdistan Region independence referendum of 25 September'; the main assault came 'in the early hours of 16 October 2017'.
16 October 2017: Kirkuk falls. 'Kirkuk city and K-1 Air Base were retaken quickly'; Iraqi forces 'seized complete control of Kirkuk province' by the end of 20 October.

region.text: Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar, with the Mosul Dam area

ledger.note: 17 October 2017: Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar. 'On 17 October the Iraqi advance continued, with gains including Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar'; Mosul Dam and other Nineveh areas followed on 18 October.

region.text: Makhmur, Zummar and the remaining disputed territories

ledger.note: 31 October 2017: the fighting ends. 'On 31 October [Abadi] announced Iraq had regained control of all disputed areas'; the Region 'lost 40% of the land mass it had administered prior to the conflict' (a later sentence: 'a fifth'). Makhmur and Zummar are not given exact dates.

wars.name: Iraqi Kurdish Civil War
wars.outcome: May 1994 to November 1997 (KDP unilateral ceasefire 24 November 1997): the KDP, dominant in Erbil and Dohuk, and the PUK, dominant in Sulaymaniyah and Halabja, fought over towns inside the Region (Shaqlawa, Chamchamal); 30,000 Iraqi troops took Erbil on 31 August 1996 and installed the KDP, then withdrew; the PUK retook Sulaymaniyah on 13 October 1996. The Washington Agreement of September 1998 ended it; the zones 'reunified in 2006'.
wars.note: The fighting was inside the Region and moved no frontier of the Region, so zones are empty; Iraq's Erbil incursion lasted days (the Kurdistan Region page does not mention it).

wars.name: 2017 Iraqi-Kurdish conflict

zones.text: the disputed territories: Kirkuk, Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa, Sinjar, Makhmur and Zummar

wars.outcome: 15-31 October 2017: Iraq retook Kirkuk (16 October), Khanaqin, Jalawla, Bashiqa and Sinjar (17 October) and the Mosul Dam (18 October); fighting at Zummar on 26 October; the Region lost 40% (or 'a fifth') of the land it administered.
wars.note: Ceasefire status of 27 October unclear on the page; Abadi ordered a 24-hour truce on border deployments.

wars.name: War in Iraq (2013-2017): Kurdish front
wars.outcome: ISIL took Sinjar in early August 2014 after the Peshmerga abandoned it; the Peshmerga offensive of 17 December 2014 ended with Sinjar retaken on 13 November 2015.
wars.note: The Northern Iraq offensive page puts the Peshmerga in Kirkuk on 13 June 2014.

certainty.note: The Region's line is a de facto military line from October 1991, called 'the Green Line' without definition on the page; the disputed territories 'remain contested' between Erbil and Baghdad. Governorate boundaries inside it are administrative.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks, written as a new dossier by me-10-x; slug used as counterpart by iraqi-republic (1992-05 loss) and republic-of-iraq (2005-10 gain; 2014-06 and 2017-10 events). Start year follows the Kurdistan Region infobox (19 May 1992); the Operation Provide Comfort page dates the Iraqi withdrawal to October 1991, so the land was stateless for seven months and the 1991 months are not drawn. Reconcile with the republic-of-iraq dossier: its 2005-10 'gain' of the Kurdistan Region would absorb the Region into Iraq on the map from 2005 to 2014; this dossier treats the Region as a separate (autonomous) state throughout and records 2005 as a status change, so the 2005 gain should be a vassal_start (federal region) or be dropped. Halabja Governorate (created later; date not on the page) is inside the Sulaymaniyah cells. Places by lon/lat radius because the gazetteer lacks them: Khanaqin/Jalawla, Bashiqa, Makhmur, Sinjar. The Kurdish civil-war split (KDP in Erbil and Duhok, PUK in Sulaymaniyah, 1994-2006) is intra-Region and drawn as one state.
